Metadata.TagValue: This role moves 1P log streams in Geneva to 3rd party customer destinations (Log Analytics, customer storage, customer EventHub)

one of the data flows of GDS, checks to determine if data being written to an LA Workspace, should also be exported to a storage account. When that is the case, GDS needs to send the data back through Normalize for ingestion in OBO, which then writes that data to a storage account.  Its called Exporter.

Metadata.TagName: How to Validate a Customer’s Data Flow Through OBO
Metadata.TagValue:
1. Identify the Customer’s First-Tag Value

    Every 1P resource that OBO reads is tagged by its ARM resource-ID (firstTagValue).

    You can find it in RegistrationTelemetry or by searching InputBlobFirstTagMetadata:

    InputBlobFirstTagMetadata | where PreciseTimeStamp > ago(1d) | where blobPath contains "your-customer-blob-path" | distinct firstTagValue

  2. Verify the Diagnostic Setting Is Registered

    RegistrationTelemetry | where PreciseTimeStamp > ago(7d) | where resourceId == "<CustomerResourceARMId>" | where dataType in ("Logs","Metrics") | project PreciseTimeStamp, resourceId, dataType, storageAccount, workspaceId, eventHubAuthorizationRuleId If no rows return, no DS exists and no data will flow.  
  3.  
    Chart the Incoming Record Volume into OBO
     
    let ft = "<CustomerFirstTagValue>"; InputBlobFirstTagMetadata | where PreciseTimeStamp > ago(6h) | where firstTagValue == ft | summarize IncomingRecords = sum(numberOfRecords) by bin(PreciseTimeStamp, 1h) | render timechart  
  4.  
    Chart the Normalized Volume (Optional)
     
    NormalizerMessageTelemetry | where PreciseTimeStamp > ago(6h) | where firstTagValue == ft | summarize BytesProcessed = sum(dataSizeInBytes), Messages = count() by bin(PreciseTimeStamp,1h) | render timechart  
  5.  
    Chart the Outgoing Success/Failure by Destination
     
    Depending on the customer’s configured destination(s), run one or more of these:
      
    Log Analytics (ODS)
     
    ODSPostTelemetry | where PreciseTimeStamp > ago(6h) | where firstPartyBlobPath contains ft | summarize SuccessCount = countif(isFailed == "False"), FailCount = countif(isFailed == "True"), TotalRecords = sum(numberOfRecords) by bin(PreciseTimeStamp,1h) | render timechart  
    Azure Storage
     
    StorageAccountAppendBlockTelemetry | where PreciseTimeStamp > ago(6h) | where firstPartyBlobPath contains ft | summarize SuccessCount = countif(isFailed == "False"), FailCount = countif(isFailed == "True"), TotalRecords = sum(numberOfRecords) by bin(PreciseTimeStamp,1h) | render timechart  
    Event Hubs
     
    EventHubSendBatchTelemetry | where PreciseTimeStamp > ago(6h) | where firstTagValue == ft | summarize SuccessCount = countif(isFailed == "false"), FailCount = countif(isFailed == "true"), TotalRecords = sum(numberOfRecords), p95 = percentile(durationInMilliseconds,95) by bin(PreciseTimeStamp,1h) | render timechart  
  6.  
    Compare Incoming vs. Outgoing
     
    If incoming ≈ outgoing (with near-zero failures), data is flowing correctly. If incoming spikes but outgoing is flat (or errors spike), you’ve found a blockage or throttle.
     
    7.   
  7.  
    Drill Into Failures (If Any)
     
    union ODSPostTelemetry | where isFailed=="True" | project PreciseTimeStamp, failureReason, workspaceId, numberOfRecords , StorageAccountAppendBlockTelemetry | where isFailed=="True" | project PreciseTimeStamp, failureReason, storageAccount, numberOfRecords , EventHubSendBatchTelemetry | where isFailed=="true" | project PreciseTimeStamp, failureReason, eventHubNamespace, numberOfRecords | where PreciseTimeStamp > ago(6h) | summarize FailureCount = count() by failureReason, bin(PreciseTimeStamp,1h) | render timechart  
  8.  
    Check OBO Service-Side Errors
     
    SvcOutgoingRequests | where PreciseTimeStamp > ago(6h) | where tostring(customDimensions.FirstTagValue) == ft | where statusCode != "200" | summarize count() by operationName, statusCode, bin(PreciseTimeStamp,1h) | render timechart This catches HTTP or RPC failures from OBO’s own outbound calls.

Summary: Lay out the charts for incoming volume, normalized volume, per-destination success/fail, and OBO service errors side by side. If all counts line up and errors are near zero, the customer’s data is flowing correctly end-to-end.

This is a web role which is the agent control channel for NSG Flow Logs. This is only used by Flow Log scenario.
This role runs background jobs (BJS) to export platform metrics to 3rd party customer destinations (Log Analytics, customer storage, customer EventHub)
This first party app is used to get credentials used to write to Customer Storage / Customer Eventhubs
This service is responsible for replicating data between the regions so that both regions are able to serve request agnostically.
